haiku-low.q1: Keys are loaded at startup, before readiness. /healthz returns 503 until all three keys are loaded, then 200.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 4 attempts total, then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. In production the rollout halts and old pods keep serving live traffic.
haiku-low.q3: Background thread re-reads every 5 minutes, swapping in changed versions. On failure it keeps the last good value and logs a warning.
haiku-low.q4: In one immutable in-memory snapshot, wrapped in a Secret type. Never in logs, disk, environment variables, or the internal endpoint.
haiku-low.q5: Only the orders-api-prod service identity can read prod values. Only the security on-call group can write them. Engineers get no access.
haiku-low.q6: Git history holds them for two years, so they count as leaked. They're harmless only once revoked at the provider after replacement.
haiku-low.q7: Each client calls secrets.get('<name>') for every outbound call and builds the Authorization header from the current in-memory snapshot.
haiku-low.q8: Each replica must run the new image and report, via an internal endpoint or metric, version ids matching those recorded in step 3.
haiku-low.q9: Store access first, then new provider keys issued, then copied into store, then app switched and config keys removed, then old keys revoked.
haiku-low.q10: Sandbox or test keys from orders-api/dev paths, fetched at startup with the engineer's own credentials. Offline runs use make run-offline with stub providers.
haiku-low.q11: Same as store unreachable: the pod retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero and never reports ready.
haiku-low.q12: No schedule is decided. Security has not decided whether or how often to rotate, and the plan picks no cadence.

sonnet.q1: Keys are loaded first; the instance is marked ready (/healthz 200) only once all three keys are loaded (503 before that).
sonnet.q2: It retries (4 attempts total, 2s apart), then exits non-zero and never becomes ready. The rollout halts and old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
sonnet.q3: A background thread re-reads the latest version of each secret every 5 minutes; if a version id differs it swaps in a new snapshot atomically. If the read fails, it keeps the last good value, logs a warning, and retries at the next tick (thread catches all exceptions).
sonnet.q4: Held in an in-memory immutable snapshot (wrapped in a Secret type that prints <redacted>). Never on disk, in environment variables, in logs (Authorization header excluded from debug logging), in tickets/chat/shell history, or in core dumps (disabled).
sonnet.q5: Read: only the service identity orders-api-prod. Write: only the security on-call group. Engineers have no prod access.
sonnet.q6: The keys remain in git history (two years), so they are treated as leaked. Each key is replaced with a new one at the provider and the old ones are revoked after all instances are confirmed on the new keys, which makes the old values harmless.
sonnet.q7: The client calls secrets.get('<name>') on each outbound call and builds the Authorization header from the current in-memory snapshot; clients no longer copy a key at construction.
sonnet.q8: Each replica reports via an internal-only endpoint/metric the version id it holds for each secret; these must match the ids recorded in step 3, and no pod from a pre-migration image may remain. Error rates and logs are also checked, and a soak window is held. Any unconfirmed replica blocks revocation.
sonnet.q9: 1) Set store access and policies; 2) issue new keys at providers (old stay active); 3) write new keys to the store; 4) pre-flight check; (dev/staging prep in parallel); 6) code PR that switches the app to the store and removes api_key lines from the config file and adds the CI guard; 7) staging drills; 8) prod rollout; 9) confirm; 10) soak; 11) inventory and revoke old keys. Rotation (new keys issued) happens early, before the app switch; revocation comes last.
sonnet.q10: From the dev store paths orders-api/dev/<name> (provider sandbox/test keys), fetched at startup with the engineer's own credentials via make run (APP_ENV=dev). Alternatively make run-offline uses local stubs with no keys. Prod access is denied.
sonnet.q11: It treats it like a failure: retries per the same sequence, then exits non-zero and never reports ready (the drill says same result as store unreachable).
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Security has not decided on a schedule or cadence; the plan picks none.
